issue.title: [Tooltip] Memory leak

labels.name: P3
labels.description: An issue that is relevant to core functions, but does not impede progress. Important, but not urgent

repository.name: components
repository.description: Component infrastructure and Material Design components for Angular

issue.body:
#### Bug:
matTooltip directive creates detatched DOM trees when used and then disposed.

If using a tooltip in an component, in my case on a normal div element, there will be a detatched dom tree for each time the view with the components including the tooltip is disposed.

After viewing and exiting a view in my application with tooltips (10 times) the following detached DOM trees could be seen:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7062803/33993264-1aba3870-e0d6-11e7-8c3f-976d133a412a.png)
(It is a comparison from two snapshots in chrome)

I narrowed the problem down and it seems like the (longpress) event in the tooltip host settings is the problem (line 91).

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7062803/33993368-7dd2fc58-e0d6-11e7-8ee2-336df7d4c179.png)

If changing this to any other event eg. keyup:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7062803/33993479-fd757e40-e0d6-11e7-96f5-514373744983.png)

Then this memory leak with detatched DOM trees are removed. I have only tested this workaround by changing in the javascript code (both es5 and es6), but I guess it should be the same if changing in the sourcecode also.

My suggestion is to either fix the longpress event or remove it until a correct longpress functionality could be made, because now the tooltip is not really usefull, not on desktop at least.
I unfortunately do not really know how a fix could be done though.

#### What are the steps to reproduce?
Create a tooltip in a component and then dispose the component. Repeat for more detached DOM trees.

https://stackblitz.com/edit/angular-g2rngj

#### Which versions of Angular, Material, OS, TypeScript, browsers are affected?
- Angular - 5.1.1
- Angular material - 5.0.1
- Chrome - Version 62.0.3202.94 (Official Build) (64-bit)

body: Looking for this fix too, is it still not merged??

issue.body:
**I'm submitting a ...** (check one with "x") [ x ] bug report [ ] feature request **Current behavior:** After playing with an application for some time, the DOM Nodes in memory stacks when navigating between components. **Expected behavior:** DOM Nodes and their references to be destroyed and released from the memory when the component is destroyed. Hi guys. We have built an app in ionic v3 with angular 5 , the issue we have is that when playing with app after some time it slows down on slow machines (Under slow machines I mean Kiosk machines with low specifications ). After some profiling and taking snapshots, it turned out that DOM Nodes are stacking up and are not cleared when the component is destroyed (e.g from Component1 navigating to Component2 -> After snapshot is taken , there are Detached nodes (Detached HTMLElements and etc.) from Component 1). At first we thought that the issues are coming from the Modal Controller ( because we do have a lot of modals in our app ) and we've updated to ionic-angular 3.9.6 - related to https://github.com/ionic-team/ionic/issues/12574. But unfortunately that didn't solve our issue. **We do use Electron for desktop app, on iOS we don't face that issue , but on Electron we do since it runs with headless chrome browser. Also this issue is reproducable after 20-30 minutes playing with the app. At first it runs smooth.** The most confusing part is that when we have the following element: `
Execute function
` after the slow down, on click the both functions (click) and (press) are executed at the same time. Unfortunately cannot share code because the app is massive but gonna mention the things we do. 1. We do use SSE (ServerSent events) 2. We do use @ViewChild() to component references with `{ read: ElementRef }` 3. We do use @Hostlisteners in the components 4. For the requests we'r using Promises 5. There are few of subscriptions but they'r unsubscribed (anyway we have 2 subscriptions in the app.component.ts) only 6. We do use `trackBy` for `ngFor` 7. We do use *ngIf with `` (e.g we don't have `Render`) 8. We do use virtual scroll for the lists. Sharing screenshots from the profiling: ![Screenshot_1](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10319093/60418860-a7202680-9bec-11e9-9e9e-08fac62d32b4.png) **The results are achieved when running **Ionic version:**

**Current behavior:**
<!-- Describe how the bug manifests. -->
DOM Nodes are stacking up in the memory.

**Expected behavior:**
<!-- Describe what the behavior would be without the bug. -->
DOM Nodes are being destroyed from the memory when the component is destroyed.

**Steps to reproduce:**
<!--  Please explain the steps required to duplicate the issue, especially if you are able to provide a sample application. -->

**NOTE: Tested the ionic 4 app with both @ionic/angular: 4.1.0 and 4.6.0 (latest version)**

2.then changed the structure in app.component.html to

```html
<ion-header>
  <ion-toolbar>
    <ion-title>Menu</ion-title>
  </ion-toolbar>
</ion-header>
<ion-content>
  <ion-list>
    <ion-menu-toggle auto-hide="false" *ngFor="let p of appPages">
      <ion-item [routerDirection]="'root'" [routerLink]="[p.url]">
        <ion-icon slot="start" [name]="p.icon"></ion-icon>
        <ion-label>
          {{p.title}}
        </ion-label>
      </ion-item>
    </ion-menu-toggle>
  </ion-list>
</ion-content>
```

3. Just open the side menu , enter Home or List page , redo that 10 , 20 times while profiling , then dont do anything... the nodes are stacking up in the memory

**NOTE: This also happened with ionic v3 starter app created**

The result: 

![ionicv4](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10319093/60655986-5e1fda80-9e57-11e9-8334-aa737e48261d.png)

Anyway, I've tested pure Angular 5 or 6 (don't remember the latest update) app that we've developed into the past, which is super massive , when ran profiling, a decrease of nodes was noticed.
